name: Scientific computing toolkit powers numerical relativity
summary: Numerical relativity is a flagship application of large-scale scientific computing: adaptive mesh refinement, high-order finite-difference and multidomain spectral solvers, constraint damping and parallel HPC turned the Einstein equations into working codes, culminating in the 2005 binary-black-hole breakthrough.
sources: Pretorius (2005). "Evolution of Binary Black-Hole Spacetimes". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 95, 121101. [arXiv:gr-qc/0507014](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0507014)

name: Machine learning for GW searches, glitches and inference
summary: Convolutional networks detect compact-binary signals and classify instrumental glitches (Gravity Spy), normalizing-flow simulation-based inference gives full posteriors in seconds, and ML surrogates of numerical-relativity waveforms speed up parameter estimation, complementing matched filtering and stochastic sampling.

name: MCMC and nested sampling for GW source parameters
summary: Posteriors over the ~15 parameters of a compact binary are sampled with Markov-chain Monte Carlo and nested sampling (LALInference, Bilby), direct descendants of the Metropolis algorithm; nested sampling also yields the Bayesian evidence used for model selection and tests of GR.
sources: Metropolis et al. (1953). "Equation of State Calculations by Fast Computing Machines". *J. Chem. Phys.* 21, 1087. [doi:10.1063/1.1699114](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1699114)

LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2016). "Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 116, 061102. [arXiv:1602.03837](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.03837)

name: Monte Carlo over geometries: causal dynamical triangulations
summary: Causal dynamical triangulations define the gravitational path integral as a sum over causal simplicial geometries, Wick-rotated and sampled by Markov-chain Monte Carlo as in lattice field theory; simulations find a phase with an extended de Sitter-like 4D geometry whose spectral dimension runs from ~4 at large scales to ~2 at short scales.

name: Well-posed hyperbolic formulations and PDE integrators
summary: The Einstein equations become a stable initial-value problem only in strongly hyperbolic formulations (generalized harmonic, BSSN with moving punctures); they are then evolved by method-of-lines Runge–Kutta with finite differences plus AMR or spectral methods, with constraint damping controlling constraint growth.
sources: Pretorius (2005). "Evolution of Binary Black-Hole Spacetimes". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 95, 121101. [arXiv:gr-qc/0507014](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0507014)

name: MERA and holographic codes as discrete AdS
summary: In a tensor network, a boundary region's entropy is bounded by the number of bonds a minimal cut crosses times log χ, a discrete Ryu–Takayanagi formula; MERA's renormalization direction resembles a hyperbolic slice of AdS (Swingle), and holographic codes built from perfect tensors model bulk reconstruction as quantum error correction.
breaks: Exact RT behaviour holds only for special (stabilizer or random) networks with flat entanglement spectra; there is no sub-AdS locality or Einstein dynamics, and MERA's emergent geometry has been argued to be closer to de Sitter or light-cone than to a spatial AdS slice.
sources: Ryu & Takayanagi (2006). "Holographic Derivation of Entanglement Entropy from AdS/CFT". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 96, 181602. [arXiv:hep-th/0603001](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0603001)

name: Hole argument and the meaning of general covariance
summary: Einstein's 1913 hole argument, in which diffeomorphism-related solutions agree outside a region but differ inside it, seemed to make generally covariant field equations indeterministic; its resolution (spacetime points have no identity apart from the metric) let Einstein accept general covariance in 1915 and started the modern substantivalism–relationism debate.

name: Problem of time in canonical quantum gravity
summary: Canonical quantization of GR gives a Hamiltonian constraint (the Wheeler–DeWitt equation) with no external time, the 'frozen formalism'; loop quantum gravity and philosophy of physics both face the task of defining dynamics through relational observables and of saying what change means in a timeless theory.

name: GR as a showcase of mathematical-physics methods
summary: GR brings many mathematical methods together: the Einstein equations as a constrained nonlinear hyperbolic PDE system, Green's-function solutions of linearized gravity, perturbation expansions (post-Newtonian, black-hole perturbation theory) and spin-weighted spherical harmonics for radiation.
sources: Einstein (1916). "Die Grundlage der allgemeinen Relativitätstheorie". *Ann. Phys.* 354, 769. [doi:10.1002/andp.19163540702](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19163540702)

name: Euclidean periodicity fixes the Hawking temperature
summary: Wick-rotating the Schwarzschild metric gives a smooth Euclidean geometry only if imaginary time is periodic with period 2πc/κ; since thermal Green's functions are periodic in imaginary time (KMS condition), that period is ħ/k_BT, which is the Hawking temperature (Gibbons–Hawking).
sources: Hawking (1975). "Particle creation by black holes". *Commun. Math. Phys.* 43, 199. [doi:10.1007/BF02345020](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02345020)

name: Ringdown quasinormal modes as Green's-function poles
summary: Black-hole ringdown is a sum of quasinormal modes: complex frequencies at the poles of the perturbation Green's function in the lower half ω-plane (plus a branch cut that gives late-time tails), computed by Leaver's continued fractions or WKB; they depend only on mass and spin, which enables black-hole spectroscopy.

name: String worldsheets as Riemann surfaces
summary: Perturbative string amplitudes are integrals over moduli spaces of Riemann surfaces; worldsheet conformal invariance makes the theory a 2D CFT, worked with holomorphic functions, contour-integral operator product expansions and modular invariance of the torus amplitude.

name: Retarded Green's function yields the quadrupole formula
summary: In Lorenz gauge, linearized gravity is a sourced wave equation for the trace-reversed perturbation; the same retarded Green's function as in electrodynamics gives the far-zone field and hence the quadrupole formula for gravitational radiation.
sources: Blanchet (2014; updated 2024). "Post-Newtonian Theory for Gravitational Waves". *Living Rev. Relativ.* [arXiv:1310.1528](https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.1528)

name: Random-subsystem entropy gives the Page curve
summary: Averaging subsystem entanglement entropy over Haar-random pure states in a finite-dimensional Hilbert space gives nearly maximal entropy for the smaller factor; applied to a black hole plus its radiation, this gives the Page curve (radiation entropy rises, then falls after the Page time), which unitarity requires and Hawking's calculation misses.
sources: Page (1993). "Information in black hole radiation". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 71, 3743. [arXiv:hep-th/9306083](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9306083)
Penington (2020). "Entanglement wedge reconstruction and the information paradox". *JHEP* 09, 002. [arXiv:1905.08255](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.08255)

name: Singularity theorems and global causal structure
summary: Global Lorentzian geometry (the Raychaudhuri focusing equation, trapped surfaces, conformal compactification into Penrose diagrams) proves that a trapped surface plus an energy condition implies geodesic incompleteness, so black-hole singularities are generic rather than artifacts of symmetry.
sources: Penrose (1965). "Gravitational Collapse and Space-Time Singularities". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 14, 57. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.14.57](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.14.57)

name: Lorentzian geometry is the language of gravity
summary: GR models gravity as curvature of a Lorentzian manifold: free fall is geodesic motion, the equivalence principle is local flatness in normal coordinates, and tidal forces are the Riemann tensor acting through geodesic deviation.
sources: Einstein (1916). "Die Grundlage der allgemeinen Relativitätstheorie". *Ann. Phys.* 354, 769. [doi:10.1002/andp.19163540702](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19163540702)

name: Contracted Bianchi identity fixes the Einstein tensor
summary: The contracted Bianchi identity makes the Einstein tensor identically divergence-free, so it can consistently be set equal to a conserved stress–energy tensor; the field equations are a statement in Riemannian geometry about Ricci curvature.

name: Petrov classification and algebraically special metrics
summary: Classifying the Weyl tensor by its principal null directions (Petrov types, Newman–Penrose formalism) organizes the exact solutions; Kerr found the rotating black hole by searching for algebraically special vacuum metrics, and the Goldberg–Sachs theorem links that degeneracy to shear-free null congruences.
sources: Kerr (1963). "Gravitational Field of a Spinning Mass as an Example of Algebraically Special Metrics". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 11, 237. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.11.237](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.11.237)

name: Lovelock's theorem defines the routes to modified gravity
summary: In four dimensions the only symmetric, divergence-free rank-2 tensor built from the metric and its first two derivatives is a combination of G_μν and g_μν; every modified-gravity theory escapes this by adding fields (scalar-tensor, Horndeski), higher derivatives (f(R)), extra dimensions or nonlocality.

name: Template-bank metric on the waveform manifold
summary: The fractional SNR lost between neighbouring templates defines a Riemannian metric on source-parameter space, and template banks are lattices laid out with this metric; the related Fisher information matrix gives forecast parameter uncertainties.

name: Ashtekar connection variables recast GR as gauge theory
summary: Rewriting canonical GR with an SU(2) connection and a densitized triad (Ashtekar, later Ashtekar–Barbero) gives it a Yang–Mills-like phase space; holonomies of the connection and fluxes of the triad are the basic variables quantized in loop quantum gravity.
sources: Ashtekar (1986). "New Variables for Classical and Quantum Gravity". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 57, 2244. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.57.2244](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.57.2244)

name: Lorentz transformations as isometries of Minkowski metric
summary: Minkowski's reformulation makes Lorentz transformations the isometries of a flat metric of Lorentzian signature; four-vectors and tensors make laws manifestly covariant, and GR reuses the same machinery for curved metrics.
sources: Einstein (1905). "Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper". *Ann. Phys.* 322, 891. [doi:10.1002/andp.19053221004](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19053221004)

name: VLBI: heterodyne receivers, maser clocks and correlators
summary: The Event Horizon Telescope is an Earth-sized interferometer: each station down-converts 1.3 mm signals with heterodyne receivers and time-stamps them with hydrogen-maser clocks, and correlators combine the recordings into visibilities whose diffraction limit resolves the ~40 μas ring; imaging is then an ill-posed inverse problem solved with regularized and Bayesian methods.
sources: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (2019). "First M87 Event Horizon Telescope Results. I. The Shadow of the Supermassive Black Hole". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 875, L1. [arXiv:1906.11238](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.11238)

name: Standard quantum limit and squeezed light in GW detectors
summary: Interferometric GW detectors are limited by fundamental instrument noise: photon shot noise and radiation-pressure noise combine into the standard quantum limit, thermal noise follows the fluctuation–dissipation theorem, and injecting squeezed vacuum (frequency-dependent since O4) beats the shot-noise limit.
sources: LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2016). "Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 116, 061102. [arXiv:1602.03837](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.03837)

name: Matched filtering and Bayesian inference of GW signals
summary: GW detection is a likelihood-ratio test built on a noise-weighted inner product (matched filtering against template banks); significance comes from time-slide background estimation, and source parameters from Bayesian posteriors.
sources: LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2016). "Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 116, 061102. [arXiv:1602.03837](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.03837)

name: Hellings–Downs correlation and Bayesian evidence in PTAs
summary: A stochastic GW background makes timing residuals correlated between pulsar pairs according to the Hellings–Downs curve; PTA collaborations weigh evidence for it with Bayes factors and frequentist statistics against common-spectrum red noise, reaching ~3–4σ significance in 2023.
sources: NANOGrav Collaboration (2023). "The NANOGrav 15 yr Data Set: Evidence for a Gravitational-wave Background". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 951, L8. [arXiv:2306.16213](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.16213)

name: CPT tests double as Lorentz-invariance tests
summary: The CPT theorem follows from Lorentz invariance plus locality, and in local interacting QFT CPT violation implies Lorentz violation; so kaon mass differences, antihydrogen spectroscopy and Penning-trap particle–antiparticle comparisons constrain Lorentz-violating coefficients of the Standard-Model Extension.
sources: Mattingly (2005). "Modern Tests of Lorentz Invariance". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 8, 5. [arXiv:gr-qc/0502097](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0502097)

name: AdS isometries equal the boundary conformal group
summary: The isometry group of AdS_{d+1} is SO(d,2), exactly the conformal group of d-dimensional Minkowski space (extended to PSU(2,2|4) for AdS5×S5 and N=4 SYM); this symmetry match underlies the bulk-field/boundary-operator dictionary, where bulk mass fixes the operator's scaling dimension.
sources: Maldacena (1998). "The Large N Limit of Superconformal Field Theories and Supergravity". *Adv. Theor. Math. Phys.* 2, 231. [arXiv:hep-th/9711200](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9711200)
Witten (1998). "Anti De Sitter Space And Holography". *Adv. Theor. Math. Phys.* 2, 253. [arXiv:hep-th/9802150](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9802150)

name: SU(2) spin networks and the quantized area spectrum
summary: LQG states are spin networks, graphs whose edges carry SU(2) irreducible representations j and whose nodes carry intertwiners; the area operator is diagonal on them with eigenvalues fixed by the SU(2) Casimir, so area is discrete.
sources: Rovelli & Smolin (1995). "Discreteness of area and volume in quantum gravity". *Nucl. Phys. B* 442, 593. [arXiv:gr-qc/9411005](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9411005)

name: Special relativity is Poincaré invariance
summary: Special relativity says physics is invariant under the Poincaré group; Wigner's unitary irreducible representations classify particles by mass and spin, and the double cover SL(2,C) of the Lorentz group gives spinors.
map: SO^+(1,3)\cong SL(2,\mathbb C)/\mathbb Z_2,\quad P^\mu P_\mu=-m^2c^2\ (\text{Casimir})
sources: Wigner (1939). "On Unitary Representations of the Inhomogeneous Lorentz Group". *Ann. Math.* 40, 149. [doi:10.2307/1968551](https://doi.org/10.2307/1968551)

name: Killing symmetries give conserved orbital constants
summary: Each Killing vector of a black-hole metric gives a quantity conserved along geodesics (energy from ∂_t, angular momentum from ∂_φ), and Komar integrals define mass and spin; Kerr also has a Killing tensor that gives the Carter constant, a hidden symmetry that makes geodesic motion integrable.

name: Diffeomorphism invariance gives local conservation
summary: Diffeomorphism invariance of the matter action implies covariant conservation of the stress–energy tensor, and invariance of the Einstein–Hilbert action implies the Bianchi identity (Noether's second theorem); globally conserved energy exists only with Killing vectors or asymptotic symmetries.
sources: Noether (1918; English translation 1971). "Invariant variation problems". *Transport Theory Stat. Phys.* 1, 186. [doi:10.1080/00411457108231446](https://doi.org/10.1080/00411457108231446)

name: No local gravitational energy; GW energy as averaged or boundary charge
summary: Because diffeomorphisms are a local gauge symmetry, Noether's second theorem gives no gauge-invariant local energy density for gravity; GW energy is defined only by averaging over wavelengths (Isaacson tensor) or as charges at null infinity, where the Bondi mass decreases as waves escape and BMS supertranslation charges are tied to the gravitational memory effect.
sources: Noether (1918; English translation 1971). "Invariant variation problems". *Transport Theory Stat. Phys.* 1, 186. [doi:10.1080/00411457108231446](https://doi.org/10.1080/00411457108231446)

name: Spontaneous Lorentz violation in the SME
summary: Lorentz symmetry could break spontaneously, with a vector or tensor field acquiring a vacuum expectation value that picks out a frame (Kostelecký–Samuel, bumblebee models); the Standard-Model Extension parametrizes the resulting background coefficients, and the associated Nambu–Goldstone modes have been proposed as photons or gravitons.
sources: Mattingly (2005). "Modern Tests of Lorentz Invariance". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 8, 5. [arXiv:gr-qc/0502097](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0502097)

name: Scale-free vacuum GR: one simulation serves all masses
summary: The vacuum Einstein equations have no intrinsic length scale, so binary-black-hole simulations are run in units of total mass M and rescale to any mass: times and lengths scale as GM/c^3 and GM/c^2, and strain is (GM/c^2)/D times a universal function. Matter breaks this scaling, which is why neutron-star mergers must be simulated separately for each equation of state.
map: t\to\lambda t,\ x\to\lambda x,\ M\to\lambda M:\quad f_{\rm GW}\propto\frac{c^3}{GM},\ h\propto\frac{GM}{c^2D}

name: Constancy of constants tests the equivalence principle
summary: Local position invariance, part of the Einstein equivalence principle, requires dimensionless constants such as α and m_p/m_e to be the same everywhere and at all times; atomic-clock comparisons, the Oklo natural reactor and quasar spectra bound their drift, and any variation would generically also violate the weak equivalence principle.
sources: Will (2014). "The Confrontation between General Relativity and Experiment". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 17, 4. [arXiv:1403.7377](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.7377)

name: Black-hole entropy is horizon area in Planck units
summary: Bekenstein–Hawking entropy is a quarter of the horizon area counted in Planck areas, and the Hawking temperature combines ħ, c, G and k_B; it is the clearest formula in which all four constants appear together, which is why black holes serve as a quantum-gravity laboratory.
sources: Bekenstein (1973). "Black Holes and Entropy". *Phys. Rev. D* 7, 2333. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333)
Hawking (1975). "Particle creation by black holes". *Commun. Math. Phys.* 43, 199. [doi:10.1007/BF02345020](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02345020)

name: Planck scale marks where quantum gravity is order one
summary: Combining G, ħ and c gives the Planck length, time and energy, where gravitational and quantum effects are both order one; every quantum-gravity programme is organized around this scale, and its ~10^15 gap above LHC energies is why direct tests are so hard.

name: Planck-suppressed dispersion and GRB time-of-flight bounds
summary: If quantum gravity changes photon dispersion at order E/E_P, high-energy photons from distant gamma-ray bursts arrive with energy-dependent delays proportional to E/E_P times the light-travel time; Fermi-LAT timing of GRB 090510 pushed the linear-order scale beyond E_P, so the Planck scale itself is now an experimentally probed quantity.
sources: Mattingly (2005). "Modern Tests of Lorentz Invariance". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 8, 5. [arXiv:gr-qc/0502097](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0502097)

name: SI second as proper time; relativistic geodesy
summary: The SI second is a proper time realized by clocks, so International Atomic Time is referred to an equipotential surface and corrected for gravitational redshift; optical clocks now resolve centimetre height differences, which turns the GR redshift into a geodesy tool and a requirement for any optical redefinition of the second.
sources: Pound & Rebka (1960). "Apparent Weight of Photons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 4, 337. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.4.337](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.4.337)

name: Hamilton–Jacobi separability and the Carter constant
summary: Carter showed that the Hamilton–Jacobi equation for Kerr geodesics separates in Boyer–Lindquist coordinates. Separation gives a fourth constant Q (from a Killing tensor) beyond μ, E and L_z, making the motion Liouville-integrable. Bound orbits therefore have action–angle variables and three fundamental frequencies, which is the basis of EMRI waveform modelling.
sources: Carter (1968). "Global Structure of the Kerr Family of Gravitational Fields". *Phys. Rev.* 174, 1559. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.174.1559](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.174.1559)

name: Hamilton–Jacobi flow as holographic renormalization
summary: Slice asymptotically AdS spacetime radially in a Hamiltonian (ADM-like) way. The on-shell gravitational action, as a functional of boundary data, then obeys a Hamilton–Jacobi equation. The radial coordinate plays the role of the renormalization scale, and the Hamiltonian constraint becomes the RG (Callan–Symanzik) equation of the dual field theory.
sources: de Boer et al. (2000). "On the holographic renormalization group". *JHEP* 08, 003. [doi:10.1088/1126-6708/2000/08/003](https://doi.org/10.1088/1126-6708/2000/08/003)

name: ADM: GR as a constrained Hamiltonian system
summary: ADM put GR in Hamiltonian form, with the spatial metric and its conjugate momentum as the canonical pair. Lapse and shift are Lagrange multipliers that enforce the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints (Dirac constrained dynamics), so the Hamiltonian vanishes on shell, as for a reparametrized particle. Numerical relativity's 3+1 evolution is built on this split and monitors the constraints.
map: H=\int d^3x\,(\alpha\mathcal H+\beta^i\mathcal H_i)+H_\partial,\ \ \mathcal H\approx0,\ \mathcal H_i\approx0,\ \ \{\gamma_{ij}(x),\pi^{kl}(y)\}=\delta_{(i}^k\delta_{j)}^l\delta^3(x-y)
breaks: Production codes (BSSN, CCZ4, generalized harmonic) reformulate the equations for strong hyperbolicity and give up the canonical structure, so constraints are damped rather than preserved symplectically.

name: Cyclic coordinates and Killing vectors for geodesics
summary: Geodesics solve the Euler–Lagrange equations of L = ½ g_μν ẋ^μ ẋ^ν. In Schwarzschild and Kerr, t and φ are cyclic coordinates, so their conjugate momenta are conserved: energy and axial angular momentum, the Noether charges of the Killing vectors ∂_t and ∂_φ. As in the Kepler problem, this reduces orbits to quadratures.
map: \mathcal L=\tfrac12g_{\mu\nu}\dot x^\mu\dot x^\nu,\ \ p_t=-E,\ p_\phi=L_z\ \text{conserved since}\ \partial_t\mathcal L=\partial_\phi\mathcal L=0

name: Least action for the metric: Einstein–Hilbert action
summary: In November 1915 Hilbert obtained the field equations by extending least action to the metric. A well-posed variational problem with fixed boundary metric needs the Gibbons–Hawking–York boundary term, and that term's Euclidean value gives the black-hole entropy.
sources: Gibbons & Hawking (1977). "Action integrals and partition functions in quantum gravity". *Phys. Rev. D* 15, 2752. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.15.2752](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.15.2752)

name: Fermat's principle: gravity as an optical medium
summary: In a static spacetime, light rays extremize optical path length (Fermat's principle in the Fermat metric). In weak fields this acts like a medium with refractive index n ≈ 1 − 2Φ/c². That index gives the 1.75″ solar deflection and lensing, and the Shapiro delay is the extra optical path.
breaks: Exact only for static (or, generalized, stationary) spacetimes; the medium is non-dispersive, and the factor 2 in n includes spatial curvature (PPN γ), so a purely Newtonian corpuscle bends only half as much.
sources: Shapiro (1964). "Fourth Test of General Relativity". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 789. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.789](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.789)

name: Crystal defects as torsion and curvature
summary: In the continuum theory of defects (Kondo, Bilby, Kröner), dislocations are the torsion and disclinations the curvature of the crystal's material connection, and Katanaev–Volovich recast defect theory as three-dimensional Riemann–Cartan gravity. Along the same lines, Sakharov's induced gravity reads the Einstein–Hilbert action as a 'metric elasticity' of the vacuum.
breaks: A crystal has a reference lattice, Euclidean signature and quadratic strain energy. Gravity has no preferred background, Lorentzian signature, and dynamics set by curvature itself. GR is torsion-free, so dislocations map to Einstein–Cartan rather than Einstein gravity.

name: Love numbers: from Earth tides to neutron-star mergers
summary: A. E. H. Love introduced dimensionless numbers for the tidal deformation of the elastic Earth. Generalized to relativistic stars, they define the tidal deformability Λ, which enters the inspiral phase at 5PN order. GW170817 bounded Λ for neutron stars and so constrained the dense-matter equation of state; black-hole Love numbers vanish in four-dimensional GR.
breaks: For neutron stars the response is dominated by the fluid interior, so Λ measures compactness and the equation of state rather than a shear modulus; crust elasticity is a small correction.
sources: Hinderer (2008). "Tidal Love Numbers of Neutron Stars". *Astrophys. J.* 677, 1216. [doi:10.1086/533487](https://doi.org/10.1086/533487)

Flanagan & Hinderer (2008). "Constraining neutron-star tidal Love numbers with gravitational-wave detectors". *Phys. Rev. D* 77, 021502. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.77.021502](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.77.021502)

name: Accretion disks as viscous Keplerian shear flows
summary: Thin accretion disks around black holes are modelled as viscous Keplerian shear flows (Shakura–Sunyaev α-disks), with turbulent stresses ν = αc_sH carrying angular momentum outward. The inner edge sits near the ISCO, which sets the radiative efficiency. Keplerian rotation is hydrodynamically Rayleigh-stable, so the turbulence must be magnetic (the magnetorotational instability).

name: Acoustic metric and analogue Hawking radiation
summary: Linear sound in an irrotational, barotropic, inviscid flow obeys a massless wave equation on an effective acoustic metric. Where the flow becomes supersonic there is a sonic horizon, whose surface gravity is set by the velocity gradient. Unruh predicted thermal phonon emission at T = ħκ/(2πk_B); the stimulated effect was seen in water waves and the spontaneous effect in BECs.
map: ds^2_{\rm ac}=\frac{\rho}{c_s}\big[-c_s^2dt^2+(d\mathbf x-\mathbf v\,dt)^2\big],\ \ T=\frac{\hbar\kappa}{2\pi k_B},\ \ \kappa=|\partial_n(c_s-v_\perp)|_{\rm hor}
breaks: Only the kinematics carries over: the acoustic metric does not obey Einstein's equations (no gravitational back-reaction), short-wavelength dispersion breaks the effective Lorentz invariance near the horizon, the fluid has a preferred frame, and the temperatures are tiny.
sources: Unruh (1981). "Experimental Black-Hole Evaporation?". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 46, 1351. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.46.1351](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.46.1351)

Weinfurtner et al. (2011). "Measurement of Stimulated Hawking Emission in an Analogue System". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 106, 021302. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.106.021302](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.106.021302)

name: Draining vortex as analogue Kerr: superradiance
summary: A draining-bathtub vortex is an analogue rotating black hole. It has an ergoregion where the flow outruns the wave speed and a horizon where the inflow does. Waves with ω < mΩ_H are amplified by extracting rotational energy, as in Zel'dovich superradiance and the Penrose process; this was observed with surface waves by Torres et al. (2017).
breaks: The effective metric is not a vacuum Einstein solution and has no inner horizon or singularity; the lab system has dissipation and dispersion, and the observed amplification used absorption at the vortex core rather than a true horizon.
sources: Torres et al. (2017). "Rotational superradiant scattering in a vortex flow". *Nature Phys.* 13, 833. [doi:10.1038/nphys4151](https://doi.org/10.1038/nphys4151)
Press & Teukolsky (1972). "Floating Orbits, Superradiant Scattering and the Black-hole Bomb". *Nature* 238, 211. [doi:10.1038/238211a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/238211a0)

name: CFD shock-capturing in relativistic hydrodynamics
summary: Numerical relativity writes the relativistic Euler/MHD equations in conservation form (the Valencia formulation) and solves them with Godunov-type high-resolution shock-capturing schemes and approximate Riemann solvers taken from CFD. This is essential for neutron-star mergers, where Kelvin–Helmholtz instability at the shear layer amplifies magnetic fields.
sources: Font (2008). "Numerical Hydrodynamics and Magnetohydrodynamics in General Relativity". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 11, 7. [doi:10.12942/lrr-2008-7](https://doi.org/10.12942/lrr-2008-7)

name: Fluid/gravity duality and the viscosity bound
summary: Long-wavelength perturbations of black-brane horizons in AdS obey the relativistic Navier–Stokes equations of the dual plasma, order by order in gradients. Transport coefficients are computed from the horizon, giving η/s = ħ/(4πk_B) for Einstein-gravity duals, a value compared with the quark–gluon plasma. The membrane paradigm anticipated this by treating the stretched horizon as a viscous fluid membrane.
sources: Bhattacharyya et al. (2008). "Nonlinear Fluid Dynamics from Gravity". *JHEP* 02, 045. [doi:10.1088/1126-6708/2008/02/045](https://doi.org/10.1088/1126-6708/2008/02/045)

Kovtun et al. (2005). "Viscosity in Strongly Interacting Quantum Field Theories from Black Hole Physics". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 94, 111601. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.94.111601](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.94.111601)

name: Gregory–Laflamme as Rayleigh–Plateau instability
summary: Black strings (Schwarzschild × a line, in D ≥ 5) are unstable to long-wavelength ripples (Gregory–Laflamme), which Cardoso–Dias mapped onto the Rayleigh–Plateau break-up of a fluid column. Numerically the string pinches self-similarly into a cascade of black-hole beads, much as fluid jets do.
breaks: Exists only in higher dimensions with extended directions. The fluid map is quantitative only in fluid/gravity or large-D limits, and the role of surface tension is played by horizon area–entropy, not by a material interface.
sources: Gregory & Laflamme (1993). "Black strings and p-branes are unstable". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 70, 2837. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.70.2837](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.70.2837)

Cardoso & Dias (2006). "Rayleigh-Plateau and Gregory-Laflamme Instabilities of Black Strings". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 96, 181601. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.181601](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.181601)

name: Holographic turbulence and AdS turbulent instability
summary: Through fluid/gravity duality, turbulent flows of a 2+1-dimensional conformal fluid correspond to dynamical AdS₄ black branes whose horizons develop fractal structure tied to the cascade. Relatedly, global AdS is weakly turbulently unstable: arbitrarily small perturbations cascade energy to ever shorter scales and collapse into black holes.
sources: Adams et al. (2014). "Holographic Turbulence". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 112, 151602. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.112.151602](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.112.151602)

Bizoń & Rostworowski (2011). "Weakly Turbulent Instability of Anti-de Sitter Spacetime". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 107, 031102. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.107.031102](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.107.031102)

name: Newtonian mechanics as the low-speed limit of SR
summary: Galilean transformations are the c→∞ contraction of Lorentz transformations, and Newton's second law, momentum and kinetic energy are the leading terms of their relativistic forms; the limit is where absolute simultaneity and separate conservation of mass are lost.
sources: Einstein (1905). "Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper". *Annalen der Physik* 322, 891. [doi:10.1002/andp.19053221004](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19053221004)

name: Effective potential: Kepler problem vs Schwarzschild
summary: Schwarzschild geodesics reduce exactly to a one-dimensional effective-potential problem like Kepler's, plus an attractive −GML²/(mc²r³) term. That term makes bound orbits precess, because the closed-orbit condition of Bertrand's theorem fails. It also removes the centrifugal barrier at small radius, which creates the innermost stable circular orbit at 6GM/c² and an unstable photon orbit at 3GM/c².
breaks: Here r is the areal radius and the radial equation is in proper time; energy enters as E², so the Newtonian total energy is recovered only in the weak-field limit.

name: Perihelion advance and light bending as orbit corrections
summary: GR adds a 3GMu²/c² term to the Kepler problem's Binet equation. Bound orbits then precess by 6πGM/[c²a(1−e²)] per orbit: 43″/century for Mercury, about 4.2°/yr periastron advance for the Hulse–Taylor pulsar, and now seen in the S2 star at Sgr A*. Unbound photon trajectories bend by 4GM/(c²b), twice the Newtonian value.
sources: Will (2014). "The Confrontation between General Relativity and Experiment". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 17, 4. [doi:10.12942/lrr-2014-4](https://doi.org/10.12942/lrr-2014-4)
Hulse & Taylor (1975). "Discovery of a pulsar in a binary system". *Astrophys. J.* 195, L51. [doi:10.1086/181708](https://doi.org/10.1086/181708)

name: Kepler orbits decaying by gravitational radiation
summary: A compact binary's inspiral is a slow sequence of Keplerian ellipses that lose energy and angular momentum to quadrupole radiation: the semimajor axis shrinks and the eccentricity decays (Peters–Mathews). The effective-one-body method extends the reduced-mass reduction of the two-body problem by mapping the relativistic binary onto a single particle in a deformed Schwarzschild metric.
sources: Peters & Mathews (1963). "Gravitational Radiation from Point Masses in a Keplerian Orbit". *Phys. Rev.* 131, 435. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.131.435](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.131.435)

Buonanno & Damour (1999). "Effective one-body approach to general relativistic two-body dynamics". *Phys. Rev. D* 59, 084006. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.59.084006](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.59.084006)

name: Conservation laws forbid monopole and dipole GWs
summary: Mass conservation and linear-momentum conservation make the monopole and mass-dipole moments radiate nothing, so the leading gravitational radiation is quadrupolar. The waves carry away energy, angular momentum (which circularizes orbits) and linear momentum; the last gives merged black holes recoil kicks of up to thousands of km/s.
map: \dot M=0,\ \ddot{\mathbf d}=\dot{\mathbf P}=0\ \Rightarrow\ P_{\rm GW}=\frac{G}{5c^5}\langle\dddot Q_{ij}\dddot Q_{ij}\rangle
sources: Campanelli et al. (2007). "Large Merger Recoils and Spin Flips from Generic Black Hole Binaries". *Astrophys. J.* 659, L5. [doi:10.1086/516712](https://doi.org/10.1086/516712)

name: Collisions and the CM frame, relativistically
summary: Newtonian collision analysis carries over to four-momentum conservation. The centre-of-mass frame becomes the frame of the invariant mass √s, and kinetic energy lost in a perfectly inelastic collision reappears as rest mass. Reaction thresholds follow from setting √s equal to the total final rest energy.
map: s=\Big(\sum E\Big)^2-\Big|\sum\mathbf pc\Big|^2,\ \ E_a^{\rm th}=\frac{(\sum m_f)^2-m_a^2-m_b^2}{2m_b}c^2
breaks: Rest mass is not separately conserved, and 'elastic' means the rest masses are unchanged rather than that kinetic energy is conserved in one frame; massless particles have no Newtonian counterpart.

name: Celestial perturbation theory and triples in GW sources
summary: Celestial mechanics' osculating-element and secular-averaging methods are used for post-Newtonian eccentric and precessing binaries. In hierarchical triples, von Zeipel–Lidov–Kozai oscillations raise the inner binary's eccentricity until gravitational radiation can merge it, a proposed channel for LIGO–Virgo mergers and for eccentric LISA sources.
sources: Blanchet (2014). "Gravitational Radiation from Post-Newtonian Sources and Inspiralling Compact Binaries". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 17, 2. [doi:10.12942/lrr-2014-2](https://doi.org/10.12942/lrr-2014-2)

Naoz (2016). "The Eccentric Kozai-Lidov Effect and Its Applications". *Annu. Rev. Astron. Astrophys.* 54, 441. [doi:10.1146/annurev-astro-081915-023315](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-astro-081915-023315)

name: Equivalence principle: tides become curvature
summary: A freely falling frame removes uniform gravity exactly, the way a change of frame removes fictitious forces. What no frame removes is the tidal tensor ∂_i∂_jΦ, which becomes the Riemann curvature in the geodesic-deviation equation. Its trace, Poisson's equation, is the Newtonian limit of the 00 Einstein equation.

name: Fictitious forces, equivalence principle, frame dragging
summary: Inertial forces in accelerating and rotating frames are proportional to inertial mass, just as gravity is proportional to gravitational mass. Einstein made this the equivalence principle, tested by Eötvös-type and MICROSCOPE experiments and by gravitational redshift. GR's gravitomagnetic field acts like a Coriolis force from local inertial frames dragged by a rotating mass (Thirring), and Gravity Probe B and LAGEOS measured it.
breaks: The equivalence is only local: no change of frame removes tidal (second-derivative) effects, and frame dragging is not a rigid global rotation, since its rate falls off as J/r³.
sources: Will (2014). "The Confrontation between General Relativity and Experiment". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 17, 4. [doi:10.12942/lrr-2014-4](https://doi.org/10.12942/lrr-2014-4)

name: Choptuik critical collapse as a saddle bifurcation
summary: Tuning initial data to the threshold between dispersal and black-hole formation drives the evolution towards a universal, discretely self-similar critical solution. In phase space this solution is a codimension-one saddle on the separatrix, and its single unstable mode λ fixes the mass-scaling exponent γ = 1/λ. This is the saddle-and-separatrix picture of bifurcation theory, with universality as in critical phenomena.
sources: Choptuik (1993). "Universality and scaling in gravitational collapse of a massless scalar field". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 70, 9. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.70.9](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.70.9)

name: Mixmaster chaos near cosmological singularities
summary: Approaching a generic spacelike singularity (BKL), Bianchi IX 'Mixmaster' spacetimes bounce through Kasner epochs governed by a map that is chaotic, like the Gauss map of continued fractions. Equivalently, the dynamics is a billiard in hyperbolic space, and coordinate-invariant fractal methods later confirmed the chaos.
breaks: Chaos in GR is coordinate-sensitive (Lyapunov exponents depend on the time variable), so gauge-invariant evidence came from fractal basin boundaries; the BKL picture for generic singularities is a conjecture supported numerically.
sources: Misner (1969). "Mixmaster Universe". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 22, 1071. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.22.1071](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.22.1071)
Cornish & Levin (1997). "The Mixmaster Universe is Chaotic". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 78, 998. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.78.998](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.78.998)

name: Kerr integrability broken: KAM and EMRI resonances
summary: Kerr geodesics are Liouville-integrable (μ, E, L_z, Carter Q), so bound orbits wind on invariant 3-tori. Perturbations break that integrability as in KAM theory, destroying resonant tori and producing islands and chaotic layers; they include the self-force, the small body's spin, external matter and non-Kerr deviations. In extreme-mass-ratio inspirals, transient r–θ resonances kick the orbital constants, which LISA waveforms must model.
sources: Flanagan & Hinderer (2012). "Transient Resonances in the Inspirals of Point Particles into Black Holes". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 109, 071102. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.109.071102](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.109.071102)

name: Inverse scattering for Einstein's equations
summary: Stationary axisymmetric vacuum Einstein equations reduce to the Ernst equation, an integrable sigma model with a Lax pair. Belinski–Zakharov applied the inverse-scattering method of KdV theory to generate 'gravitational solitons', and Kerr arises as a two-soliton solution on flat space. Bäcklund transformations and the Geroch group generate further exact solutions.
map:

abla\mathcal E\cdot
abla\mathcal E,\ \ \mathcal E=f+i\psi;\ \ 	ext{Kerr}=	ext{2-soliton solution}
breaks: Gravitational solitons are solitons in the formal inverse-scattering sense (pole insertions in the dressing matrix), not localized waves that keep their shape through collisions.
sources: Ernst (1968). "New Formulation of the Axially Symmetric Gravitational Field Problem". *Phys. Rev.* 167, 1175. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.167.1175](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.167.1175)

name: Black-hole quasinormal modes as damped normal modes
summary: Linear perturbations of Schwarzschild and Kerr reduce to one-dimensional wave equations with a potential barrier near the photon sphere. The ringdown is a sum of quasinormal modes: damped 'normal modes' whose complex frequencies are fixed by mass and spin alone. For example, Mω ≈ 0.374 − 0.089i for the fundamental ℓ=2 Schwarzschild mode (G=c=1), so Q ≈ 2.
breaks: The system is open, since waves leak to infinity and into the horizon. The problem is therefore non-self-adjoint and quasinormal modes are not a complete orthogonal basis. The signal also has a prompt part and late-time power-law tails that no mode sum captures.
sources: Berti et al. (2009). "Quasinormal modes of black holes and black branes". *Class. Quantum Grav.* 26, 163001. [doi:10.1088/0264-9381/26/16/163001](https://doi.org/10.1088/0264-9381/26/16/163001)
Vishveshwara (1970). "Scattering of Gravitational Radiation by a Schwarzschild Black-hole". *Nature* 227, 936. [doi:10.1038/227936a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/227936a0)

name: Pendulum suspensions, Q and thermal noise in LIGO
summary: Interferometer mirrors hang as pendulums with f₀ ~ 1 Hz, so above resonance they respond as free masses. Cascaded suspension stages filter seismic motion as ∏(f_k/f)², and fluctuation–dissipation sets suspension thermal noise, which is why ultra-high-Q fused-silica fibres are used. Weber's resonant bars had earlier used a high-Q driven oscillator directly as the detector.
sources: Saulson (1990). "Thermal noise in mechanical experiments". *Phys. Rev. D* 42, 2437. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.42.2437](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.42.2437)
Weber (1960). "Detection and Generation of Gravitational Waves". *Phys. Rev.* 117, 306. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.117.306](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.117.306)

name: Lighthill's acoustic quadrupole and GW quadrupole
summary: In Lighthill's acoustic analogy, free turbulence radiates sound as a quadrupole because mass and momentum conservation remove monopole and dipole sources. Gravitational radiation is quadrupolar for the same reason. Both are sourced by a stress-type tensor, and the radiated power scales as the squared third time derivative of the quadrupole.
breaks: Sound is a scalar wave in a medium with a rest frame, and monopole or dipole sound returns whenever mass is injected or boundaries exert force. Gravitational waves are spin-2 waves of spacetime itself, and no isolated system can evade the quadrupole rule.
sources: Lighthill (1952). "On sound generated aerodynamically I. General theory". *Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A* 211, 564. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1952.0060](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1952.0060)

name: Seismic and acoustic Newtonian noise in GW detectors
summary: Seismic surface (Rayleigh) waves and atmospheric infrasound change the local mass density, and the resulting fluctuations in Newtonian gravity pull on the test masses directly, bypassing seismic isolation. This sets a low-frequency wall below about 10 Hz. It motivates underground sites such as the Einstein Telescope and seismometer arrays for Wiener-filter subtraction.
map: \delta\mathbf g(\mathbf r,t)=-G\int\frac{\delta\rho(\mathbf r',t)\,(\mathbf r-\mathbf r')}{|\mathbf r-\mathbf r'|^3}\,d^3r'
sources: Hughes & Thorne (1998). "Seismic gravity-gradient noise in interferometric gravitational-wave detectors". *Phys. Rev. D* 58, 122002. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.58.122002](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.58.122002)
Saulson (1984). "Terrestrial gravitational noise on a gravitational wave antenna". *Phys. Rev. D* 30, 732. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.30.732](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.30.732)

name: Vibrating string and the relativistic string
summary: The relativistic string's Nambu–Goto action is the worldsheet area, the analogue of a particle's proper time. In conformal gauge it gives the one-dimensional wave equation of a stretched string. The Fourier normal modes become oscillators whose quantized excitation number N sets the mass spectrum, so the string's particle content is the normal-mode spectrum of a vibrating string.
map: S_{\rm NG}=-T\int d\tau\,d\sigma\sqrt{(\dot X\cdot X')^2-\dot X^2X'^2},\ \ (\partial_\tau^2-\partial_\sigma^2)X^\mu=0,\ \ \alpha'M^2=N-1
breaks: The relativistic string has only transverse physical modes (the Virasoro constraints remove the rest), and its tension equals its mass per length, so waves travel at c. Quantum consistency also fixes the spacetime dimension (26 or 10). None of this holds for a guitar string.

name: Acoustic vs relativistic Doppler effect
summary: The acoustic Doppler shift depends separately on source and observer speeds relative to the medium. The relativistic shift depends only on their relative velocity and includes a purely transverse redshift from time dilation, measured by Ives–Stilwell. Historically, Voigt (1887) found Lorentz-like transformations by demanding invariance of the wave equation.
breaks: Sound has a preferred frame (the medium); only the linear acoustic wave equation has a Lorentz-like symmetry with c_s, while the fluid itself is Galilean, which is also why analogue spacetimes hold only for perturbations.
sources: Ives & Stilwell (1938). "An Experimental Study of the Rate of a Moving Atomic Clock". *J. Opt. Soc. Am.* 28, 215. [doi:10.1364/JOSA.28.000215](https://doi.org/10.1364/JOSA.28.000215)

name: Parametric instability and optical springs in LIGO
summary: At high circulating power, radiation pressure couples a mirror's acoustic mode to two optical cavity modes. When their frequency difference matches the acoustic frequency and the parametric gain R exceeds 1, the acoustic mode rings up exponentially, as in a pumped parametric oscillator; Advanced LIGO first observed this in 2014. Radiation pressure also acts as an optical spring that shifts the test-mass dynamics and can destabilize them.
sources: Evans et al. (2015). "Observation of Parametric Instability in Advanced LIGO". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 114, 161102. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.114.161102](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.114.161102)

name: Cosmological particle creation as parametric amplification
summary: Each Fourier mode of a quantum field in an expanding universe is an oscillator with a time-dependent frequency. Non-adiabatic changes mix positive and negative frequencies (Bogoliubov coefficients β_k), which is parametric amplification seeded by vacuum fluctuations. In preheating, the inflaton's oscillations turn the mode equation into a Mathieu equation whose instability bands create particles explosively.
sources: Parker (1969). "Quantized Fields in Expanding Universes. I". *Phys. Rev.* 183, 1057. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.183.1057](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.183.1057)
Kofman et al. (1994). "Reheating after Inflation". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 73, 3195. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.73.3195](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.73.3195)

name: Gyroscope precession as a test of GR (Gravity Probe B)
summary: A free gyroscope's spin is parallel-transported along its orbit, so in curved spacetime it precesses relative to the distant stars. There are two terms: geodetic (de Sitter) precession from space curvature and Lense–Thirring frame dragging from Earth's spin. Gravity Probe B measured 6601.8±18.3 and 37.2±7.2 mas/yr, against GR's 6606.1 and 39.2 mas/yr.
sources: Everitt et al. (2011). "Gravity Probe B: Final Results of a Space Experiment to Test General Relativity". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 106, 221101. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.106.221101](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.106.221101)

name: Spin precession of compact binaries
summary: In spinning compact binaries, spin–orbit coupling makes the orbital angular momentum L and the spins precess around a nearly fixed total J, like coupled gyroscopes. This is simple precession, with a transitional regime when L ≈ −S. The precession cone modulates the gravitational-wave amplitude and phase.
map: \dot{\mathbf L}=\boldsymbol\Omega_p\times\mathbf L,\ \ \dot{\mathbf S}=\boldsymbol\Omega_p\times\mathbf S,\ \ \mathbf J=\mathbf L+\mathbf S\approx\text{const}
breaks: The torque is the relativistic (gravitomagnetic) spin–orbit coupling, not a Newtonian torque on a lopsided body, and J itself slowly shrinks as radiation carries angular momentum away.
sources: Apostolatos et al. (1994). "Spin-induced orbital precession and its modulation of the gravitational waveforms from merging binaries". *Phys. Rev. D* 49, 6274. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.49.6274](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.49.6274)

name: Thomas precession: Lorentz kinematics of spin
summary: Two non-collinear Lorentz boosts compose to a boost plus a rotation (Wigner rotation), so a gyroscope or spin carried along an accelerated path precesses even in flat spacetime. Thomas precession supplies the factor ½ in atomic spin–orbit coupling and enters the BMT equation used for spin precession in storage rings such as muon g−2.
sources: Thomas (1926). "The Motion of the Spinning Electron". *Nature* 117, 514. [doi:10.1038/117514a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/117514a0)

Bargmann et al. (1959). "Precession of the Polarization of Particles Moving in a Homogeneous Electromagnetic Field". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 2, 435. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.2.435](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.2.435)

name: Inertia tensor, mass quadrupole and spinning-star GWs
summary: The trace-free mass quadrupole that sources gravitational waves is minus the trace-free inertia tensor. A rigid body spinning about a principal axis therefore radiates only if it is non-axisymmetric (I₁≠I₂), at twice the spin frequency, with amplitude ∝ εI₃f². Euler free precession (wobble) adds emission near the spin frequency. This is the basis of continuous-wave searches for neutron-star 'mountains'.
sources: Zimmermann & Szedenits (1979). "Gravitational waves from rotating and precessing rigid bodies: Simple models and applications to pulsars". *Phys. Rev. D* 20, 351. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.20.351](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.20.351)

name: Hellings–Downs curve as a spatial coherence function
summary: A stochastic GW background is a Gaussian random field that, like partially coherent light, can only be detected by cross-correlating separated receivers; the Hellings–Downs curve is the angular correlation of pulsar timing residuals for an isotropic spin-2 background, the analogue of the mutual coherence function versus baseline.
map: \Gamma(\zeta)=\tfrac32x\ln x-\tfrac{x}{4}+\tfrac12,\ x=\tfrac{1-\cos\zeta}{2}\ \leftrightarrow\ \Gamma_{12}(\mathbf b)\propto\int I(\hat s)e^{-ik\mathbf b\cdot\hat s}d\Omega
breaks: The correlated quantity is a redshift integrated along the line of sight with a quadrupolar spin-2 response, not a field amplitude at a point; pulsar terms add uncorrelated noise, and a background from a finite source population has cosmic variance.

name: Aperture synthesis images black-hole shadows
summary: Each VLBI baseline samples one spatial-frequency component of the sky brightness (van Cittert–Zernike), so the Earth-sized EHT is a sparse Fourier-plane aperture whose image is recovered by regularized inversion at λ/D ≈ 20 μas; the ~42 μas ring of M87* tests the predicted Kerr shadow size.

Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (2019). "First M87 Event Horizon Telescope Results. IV. Imaging the Central Supermassive Black Hole". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 875, L4. [doi:10.3847/2041-8213/ab0e85](https://doi.org/10.3847/2041-8213/ab0e85)

name: Eikonal limit: null geodesics, photon sphere, shadow
summary: The short-wavelength limit of Maxwell's equations on a curved background gives rays along null geodesics, with a parallel-transported wave vector and conserved photon number; the photon sphere at 3GM/c² and the critical impact parameter √27 GM/c² that sets the shadow are geometric-optics results, computed by backward ray tracing.

name: Weak-field lensing as an effective refractive index
summary: In a weak static field light moves as if in a medium of index n = 1 − 2Φ/c², so Fermat's principle gives the deflection 4GM/(c²b), twice the Newtonian value, and the Shapiro delay is the excess optical path; the lens equation is ray optics with an achromatic thin lens.
breaks: Valid only for weak, static fields; the index is achromatic and comes half from time curvature and half from space curvature (PPN γ); strong fields need full null geodesics.

name: Wave-optics (diffractive) lensing of gravitational waves
summary: When a GW's wavelength is comparable to the Schwarzschild radius of a lens, geometric optics fails and the Fresnel–Kirchhoff diffraction integral gives a frequency-dependent amplification factor that imprints interference and diffraction on the waveform; this is a target for searches in LIGO and LISA data.
map: F(w,\mathbf y)=\frac{w}{2\pi i}\int d^2x\,e^{iwT(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)},\quad w=\frac{4GM_{Lz}\,\omega}{c^3}

name: Michelson interferometry reads out spacetime strain
summary: LIGO, Virgo and KAGRA are Michelson interferometers held near a dark fringe; a passing wave changes the differential arm length by ΔL = hL, which appears as an output phase shift amplified by Fabry–Pérot arm cavities and recycling to reach strain noise ~10^-23/√Hz.
sources: Abbott et al. (2016). "Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 116, 061102. [arXiv:1602.03837](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.03837)

name: Time-delay interferometry for unequal-arm LISA
summary: LISA's 2.5 million km arms cannot be held equal, so laser frequency noise would swamp the signal; LISA records one-way heterodyne phases between spacecraft and recombines them in post-processing with time shifts (TDI) to synthesize equal-arm Michelson and Sagnac interferometers.

name: Michelson–Morley null ether-drift interferometer
summary: The 1887 interferometer looked for a fringe shift ∝ (v/c)²L/λ on rotation, caused by Earth's motion through the ether, and saw less than about a twentieth of the expected 0.4 fringe; the result was a key empirical input to special relativity and the template for every later two-arm isotropy test.
sources: Michelson & Morley (1887). "On the Relative Motion of the Earth and the Luminiferous Ether". *Am. J. Sci.* 34, 333. [doi:10.2475/ajs.s3-34.203.333](https://doi.org/10.2475/ajs.s3-34.203.333)
Mattingly (2005). "Modern Tests of Lorentz Invariance". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 8, 5. [arXiv:gr-qc/0502097](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0502097)

name: EHT polarimetry maps horizon-scale magnetic fields
summary: Stokes-parameter imaging of the synchrotron emission from M87* and Sgr A* shows ordered spiral linear polarization; the pattern and its Faraday rotation through the magnetized accretion flow constrain the field geometry and favour magnetically arrested disks.

name: Plus/cross: spin-2 analogue of linear polarization
summary: GWs have two transverse polarizations (+, ×) that, like light's two linear states, combine into circular helicity states and admit Stokes-like parameters for stochastic backgrounds; but + and × differ by a 45° rotation, not 90°, because a rotation by ψ multiplies helicity-h amplitudes by e^{ihψ}.
map: h_+\pm ih_\times\to e^{\pm2i\psi}(h_+\pm ih_\times)\ \leftrightarrow\ E_x\pm iE_y\to e^{\pm i\psi}(E_x\pm iE_y)
breaks: A tensor wave produces a quadrupolar tidal strain on a ring of test masses rather than a force on a charge, and there is essentially no gravitational medium, so GR has no counterpart of crystal birefringence.

name: Vacuum birefringence as a Lorentz-violation probe
summary: Lorentz-violating photon terms (SME k_F, Carroll–Field–Jackiw) make the vacuum birefringent, so polarization rotates or splits in proportion to distance and frequency; polarimetry of gamma-ray bursts, AGN and the CMB constrains these coefficients to the 10^-32 level and below.
sources: Colladay & Kostelecký (1998). "Lorentz-violating extension of the standard model". *Phys. Rev. D* 58, 116002. [doi:10.1103/physrevd.58.116002](https://doi.org/10.1103/physrevd.58.116002)

name: Maxwell's equations force special relativity
summary: Maxwell's equations are invariant under Lorentz, not Galilean, transformations; the moving-magnet/conductor asymmetry and null ether-drift experiments led Lorentz, Poincaré and Einstein ('On the electrodynamics of moving bodies', 1905) to rebuild kinematics around an invariant c, which then fixed the form of every later field theory.
map: c=1/\sqrt{\mu_0\epsilon_0}\ \text{in every inertial frame}\Rightarrow x'^\mu=\Lambda^\mu{}_\nu x^\nu
sources: Einstein (1905). "Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper". *Ann. Phys.* 322, 891. [doi:10.1002/andp.19053221004](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19053221004)
Michelson & Morley (1887). "On the Relative Motion of the Earth and the Luminiferous Ether". *Am. J. Sci.* 34, 333. [doi:10.2475/ajs.s3-34.203.333](https://doi.org/10.2475/ajs.s3-34.203.333)

name: Gertsenshtein effect: graviton–photon conversion
summary: A GW crossing a static magnetic field sources an EM wave of the same frequency through the field's stress–energy coupling (Gertsenshtein 1962), and vice versa; this mixing underlies proposals to detect MHz–GHz gravitational waves with strong magnets and microwave cavities like those of axion haloscopes.

name: Interstellar plasma dispersion in pulsar timing
summary: Radio pulses crossing ionized interstellar plasma travel at a group velocity set by the plasma frequency (the same dispersion relation as a waveguide above cutoff) and arrive late by an amount ∝ DM/f²; PTAs observe at several frequencies to fit and remove this chromatic delay, a dominant noise in nanohertz GW searches.

name: Dynamical Casimir effect and moving-mirror radiation
summary: Time-dependent boundary conditions on a cavity or transmission line mix positive and negative frequencies and create photon pairs from vacuum; this is the moving-mirror model (Fulling–Davies) that reproduces Hawking's thermal flux, and it was observed in 2011 with a SQUID-modulated superconducting transmission line.

name: Rotating resonant cavities as modern Michelson–Morley
summary: Modern isotropy tests compare the resonance frequencies of orthogonal cryogenic optical or microwave cavities on rotating platforms; any direction dependence of c shifts their beat note, which bounds photon-sector Standard-Model-Extension coefficients near the 10^-17–10^-18 level.
sources: Mattingly (2005). "Modern Tests of Lorentz Invariance". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 8, 5. [arXiv:gr-qc/0502097](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0502097)
Colladay & Kostelecký (1998). "Lorentz-violating extension of the standard model". *Phys. Rev. D* 58, 116002. [doi:10.1103/physrevd.58.116002](https://doi.org/10.1103/physrevd.58.116002)

name: Blandford–Znajek: spinning hole as unipolar inductor
summary: A Kerr black hole threaded by magnetic flux behaves like Faraday's spinning-disk dynamo: frame dragging drives an EMF across field lines, currents close through the force-free magnetosphere and the horizon's resistance, and rotational energy leaves as Poynting flux; this is the leading model for jets from magnetically arrested disks.
sources: Blandford & Znajek (1977). "Electromagnetic extraction of energy from Kerr black holes". *Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc.* 179, 433. [doi:10.1093/mnras/179.3.433](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/179.3.433)

name: Gravitoelectromagnetism and frame dragging
summary: For weak fields and slow sources the metric perturbations h_00 and h_0i act as gravito-electric and gravito-magnetic potentials obeying Maxwell-like equations sourced by mass density and mass current; frame dragging (Lense–Thirring, measured by Gravity Probe B and LAGEOS) is the gravitomagnetic field of a spinning mass.
map: h_{00}\leftrightarrow\phi,\ h_{0i}\leftrightarrow A_i,\ \rho\leftrightarrow\rho_q,\ \rho\mathbf v\leftrightarrow\mathbf J,\ \epsilon_0\to-1/(4\pi G)
breaks: Holds only at linear order and for slow motion; factors of 2 and 4 depend on convention because the source is a spin-2 tensor; like masses attract, there are no negative masses or gravitational dipole radiation, and full GR is nonlinear.

name: Gauge connections: vector potential vs Christoffel
summary: The vector potential is a U(1) connection whose curvature is F and whose holonomy is the Aharonov–Bohm phase; in GR the Christoffel (or spin) connection plays the same role, Riemann is its curvature, and parallel transport around a loop measures it, so both are theories of connections on bundles.
breaks: Gravity gauges spacetime itself (diffeomorphisms) and adds a metric/tetrad with no Maxwell counterpart; the Einstein–Hilbert action is linear in curvature while Maxwell's is quadratic, and there is no fixed background.

name: Proca photon vs massive graviton (Stückelberg, vDVZ)
summary: A photon mass breaks gauge invariance, but the massless limit is smooth because the Stückelberg scalar decouples; the same Stückelberg trick applied to Fierz–Pauli massive gravity exposes a helicity-0 mode that does not decouple (vDVZ discontinuity), cured nonlinearly by Vainshtein screening and dRGT; both masses are bounded by wave dispersion (m_γ ≲ 10^-18 eV, m_g ≲ 10^-23 eV).
breaks: The spin-1 massless limit is continuous and the spin-2 one is not: the graviton's scalar mode couples to T and changes linear-order light bending to 3/4 of the GR value; massive gravity also has the Boulware–Deser ghost, which Proca lacks.
